Write MVT, IVT, FTC explicitly when applying them
Always include correct units in applied problems
Round to 3 decimal places only at the final step

figure.title: Particle Velocity and Sign Changes: v(t) = t² - 4t + 3

caption.en: Velocity $v(t) = (t-1)(t-3)$ for particle motion. The particle is moving right when $v(t) > 0$ on $[0,1) \cup (3,\infty)$, and moving left when $v(t) < 0$ on $(1,3)$. Total distance requires integrating the speed $|v(t)|$.

body.en:
A particle moves along a line with velocity \( v(t)=t^2-4t+3 \) for \( t\geq 0 \).

(a) When is the particle at rest? \( v(t)=(t-1)(t-3)=0 \Rightarrow t=1,\ 3 \).

(b) On \( [0,3] \), when is it moving left? \( v<0 \) on \( (1,3) \), so it moves left there (and right on \( [0,1) \)).

(c) Total distance travelled on \( [0,3] \):

\[ \int_0^3 |v(t)|\,dt=\Big|\!\int_0^1 v\,\Big|+\Big|\!\int_1^3 v\,\Big|=\tfrac43+\tfrac43=\tfrac83. \]

Let \( R \) be the region bounded by \( y=\sqrt{x} \) and \( y=x \).

(a) Area of \( R \) (here \( \sqrt{x}\geq x \) on \( [0,1] \)):

\[ \int_0^1\big(\sqrt{x}-x\big)\,dx=\Big[\tfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}-\tfrac{x^2}{2}\Big]_0^1=\tfrac23-\tfrac12=\tfrac16. \]

(b) Volume when \( R \) is revolved about the \( x \)-axis (washers):

\[ \pi\int_0^1\big[(\sqrt{x})^2-x^2\big]\,dx=\pi\int_0^1\big(x-x^2\big)\,dx=\frac{\pi}{6}. \]

label.en: FRQ 3 · Rate In / Rate Out Accumulation Model

body.en:
Water enters a municipal reservoir at a rate modelled by \( R(t) = 200 + 40\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{12}\right) \) gallons/hour and is pumped out at a constant rate of \( L(t) = 180 \) gallons/hour for \( 0 \leq t \leq 24 \) hours. At \( t = 0 \), the reservoir contains \( 1200 \) gallons.

(a) Amount of water entering: The total water added on \( [0, 8] \) is \( \int_0^8 R(t)\,dt \approx 1845.672 \text{ gallons} \).

(b) Rate of change of volume: At \( t = 6 \), the net rate of change is \( V'(6) = R(6) - L(6) = \left[200 + 40\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right] - 180 = 240 - 180 = 60 \text{ gal/hr} \). Because \( V'(6) > 0 \), the amount of water in the reservoir is increasing at \( t = 6 \).

(c) Absolute Extrema (Candidates Test): The total volume is \( V(t) = 1200 + \int_0^t [R(u) - L(u)]\,du \). Critical points occur where \( V'(t) = R(t) - L(t) = 0 \Rightarrow 200 + 40\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{12}\right) = 180 \Rightarrow \sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{12}\right) = -0.5 \Rightarrow \frac{\pi t}{12} = \frac{7\pi}{6} \Rightarrow t = 14 \). Evaluate candidates: \( V(0) = 1200 \), \( V(14) \approx 1895.348 \), and \( V(24) \approx 1680 \). By the Candidates Test, the maximum volume is approximately \( 1895.348 \text{ gallons} \) at \( t = 14 \text{ hours} \).

label.en: ⚠️ AP Reader Scoring Traps & FRQ Writing Conventions

body.en:
• The Pronoun 'It' Penalty: Never write 'it is increasing because it is positive'. AP readers do not assume what 'it' refers to. Always explicitly name the function and derivative: 'The function \( f \) is increasing on \( (a, b) \) because \( f'(x) > 0 \).'
  • Candidates Test Format: To justify an absolute extremum on a closed interval \( [a, b] \), you must explicitly evaluate and compare \( f(x) \) at all interior critical numbers AND both boundary endpoints. Showing that \( f' \) changes sign is only valid for local extrema, not absolute extrema on an interval with endpoints!
  • Separate Units Point: AP free-response parts frequently include an independent point just for correct units (e.g. \( \text{ft/sec}^2 \) vs \( \text{ft/sec} \)). Always check the problem stem for 'using correct units, explain the meaning of...' and provide units even if you had difficulty with earlier arithmetic.
  • Never Round Intermediate Calculations: Store full decimal values in your calculator. Only round or truncate to 3 decimal places at your final stated answer.
